header:
Date: 2026-07-24
Time: 14:00 PT (approx 42 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE); Asha Patel (VP Eng), Marc Lebrun (Platform), Sanjay Rao (Security)
Recording: Fireflies transcript export
Links/Shared: onboarding-playbook-v1 (drive), security-pack (link), perf-spreadsheet (link)
summary: Intro to the onboarding plan, network and security constraints clarified, decision to pilot on Dedicated capacity with a 2-week perf benchmark. Action items assigned for SAML + perf checklist and data classification.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Asha (Praxis): Hi all, Asha here. Thanks, yeah quick intro, Marc and Sanjay from my team on the call.
[00:20] Marc (Praxis): Morning, Marc.
[00:24] Sanjay (Praxis): Hey — good to meet you.
[00:28] Maya (Redwood CSM): Hey, Maya here, I'll be your customer success lead; I'll run the onboarding cadence.
[00:33] Luis (Redwood SE): Luis, infra/SE. I'll own the perf and network stuff.
[00:38] Jordan: Great. Goal for today: align on constraints, decide initial deployment pattern, and pick pilot scope.
[01:05] Asha: High-level — Praxis is integrating Redwood to power our in-app assistants and some internal summarization. Our constraints: PCI-ish data classification for certain tokens, we have to keep logs retention to 90 days or less, and egress needs to be restricted to our peered VPCs.
[01:36] Jordan: Got it. So sounds like Private or Dedicated makes sense given data constraints, correct?
[01:45] Asha: Yes, leaning Dedicated. We want isolation and predictable latency. Also — SSO is mandatory, SAML, and audit logs to feed into our SIEM.
[02:05] Luis: Quick clarifying q: when you say egress restricted, is that full deny except to specific endpoints, or allowed to a couple of external blob storage endpoints?
[02:18] Marc: Full deny except our S3-compatible storage and our internal metrics endpoint. No public egress from the nodes.
[02:27] Luis: Ok that maps. We'll document necessary NAT / VPC peering requirements.
[03:00] Jordan: On the product side: Redwood Dedicated will give you reserved pools and predictable throughput; Private (VPC) option is also possible if you want a customer-managed control plane. For pilot, Dedicated with VPC peering usually hits the sweet spot.
[03:22] Asha: One question — latency targets. We care about 95th percentile < 200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) for chat use. Is that realistic?
[03:35] Luis: 200ms p95 is aggressive depending on model size and batch tuning. For small models or quantized variants, yes. For larger ones (13B+) you'd see higher numbers unless we tune batching and KV cache. We can target sub-200ms with a tuned setup. We'll need to run a short benchmark.
[04:05] Sanjay: Security: SOC 2 is a must, we need evidence of key management — integration with our KMS for envelope encryption, and control over logs. Also IP allowlists and RBAC.
[04:23] Maya: We have a security pack; Jordan, I'll share the pack and the SOC docs after the call. There's a checklist item in the pack for KMS integrations.
[04:40] Jordan: Yeah we'll include our SOC 2 attestation and a walkthrough for the KMS options (KMS or HSM via partner).
[05:00] Marc: On capacity — initial traffic estimate: 50 qps during business hours on average, bursting to 150 qps; initial footprint should support latency targets.
[05:15] Luis: That helps. For Reserved Dedicated pools we'd size based on peak tokens/sec — I'll propose three configurations in the perf plan: baseline (minimal), mid, and enterprise. We'll run simulations in the benchmark.
[05:40] Jordan: Timeline — Praxis wants an internal pilot in August, production by mid-September ideally. Is that feasible?
[05:51] Asha: Pilot in August is the ask — yes.
[05:55] Luis: We can aim for a pilot cluster provisioned in early August if networking and SSO are quick.
[06:10] Jordan: Ok next, network items: we'll need an inventory of IPs to allow, and Marc, can you share your VPC peering team contact?
[06:20] Marc: Sure, I'll share the network diagram after the call.
[06:25] Jordan: Great — action item noted.
[06:50] [08:00] Jordan: Let's talk about data retention and logs — Praxis wants 90-day retention and full audit trails. We support export of logs and can integrate with your SIEM. The default hosted logs are longer; we'll ensure Dedicated keeps logs per your retention through config.
[08:22] Sanjay: We also need to redact PII tokens before logs are persisted; is there a runtime redact or we should implement at application layer?
[08:33] Luis: We have prefix/KV caching and some pre-processing hooks. For compliance we typically recommend app-layer token filtering before sending to the model, but we can set up a post-processing scrubber as a guardrail. We'll include guidance in the security pack.
[09:00] Asha: Will Redwood integrate with our KMS for customer-managed keys?
[09:06] Maya: Short answer yes — we support external KMS through the Private offering and in Dedicated we have KMS integrations too. We'll follow up with details.
[09:20] Jordan: Now about models — do you plan to use open models or Redwood-verified models?
[09:29] Marc: We prefer open LLMs to avoid vendor lock-in, but we need model performance guarantees. If Redwood has verified performance profiles, that helps.
[09:41] Luis: We maintain a catalog and performance profiles; for the pilot we can propose a quantized 13B or 7B variant depending on your latency goals. We'll include recommended quantization and kernel selections in the perf checklist.
[10:05] [12:10] Jordan: Competitors — I know you evaluated Anthropic and ApexCloud, any features that tipped towards them?
[10:18] Asha: Anthropic's safety toolkit was compelling, ApexCloud had competitive pricing. Our focus is reliability and audits though.
[10:28] Jordan: Ok noted.
[10:34] [13:00] Luis: Perf benchmark plan — what we propose: 1) baseline synthetic load to validate p95 latency, 2) replay of a small sample of your production-ish traces (sanitized), 3) edge-case tests for long-context sessions. Need access to sample traces or representative traffic.
[11:02] Asha: We can provide a 24-hour sampled trace, sanitized, by next Friday.
[11:10] Luis: Perfect — that'll help size autoscale thresholds and batching configs.
[11:25] [15:00] Maya: Onboarding cadence — I suggest weekly check-ins for the first 3 weeks, then biweekly during the pilot. We'll use a shared drive and the onboarding-playbook doc.
[11:44] Asha: Weekly works.
[11:50] Jordan: About billing/pricing — we can offer a pilot pricing construct or a short-term committed capacity discount; I'll share options.
[12:02] Marc: For procurement, we may need a PO and SOW for the pilot. Any templates?
[12:10] Maya: We'll attach a standard pilot SOW template in the drive.
[12:20] [20:00] Sanjay: A question on backups and snapshots of models — do you keep model artifacts accessible and how are updates rolled out?
[12:33] Luis: Models are versioned. We can pin a model version for the pilot and we support canary deployments for rollouts. Backups for the model artifacts live in immutable storage with access controls. We'll document the rollout flow.
[12:50] Asha: Ok that's good.
[13:05] [25:00] Jordan: Any blockers from your side that would prevent an early August pilot?
[13:12] Marc: Main blocker is network approvals — usually 5-7 business days. If we get Jordan's network checklist today, we can queue it.
[13:22] Asha: Also SAML SSO config will need our IdP team time; we'll try to prioritize.
[13:30] Jordan: I'll send the SAML guide and network checklist right after.
[13:40] Maya: We'll also start the onboarding workspace and invite your team.
[13:50] [33:00] Luis: I'll draft the performance plan with three sizing options and share the perf checklist and test vectors.
[14:05] Asha: One more thing — compliance review, can you share your audit logs schema so we can validate retention and fields?
[14:13] Jordan: Yes — that's part of the security pack I'll drop.
[14:20] [35:00] Marc: Thanks everyone — this has been helpful.
[14:25] Jordan: Quick recap — Jordan sends SAML + network diagram + security pack (due 7/28), Luis shares perf plan and checklist (due 8/3), Asha provides sanitized trace and data classification (due 7/30). Schedule pilot for week of 8/10 pending approvals. Weekly check-ins starting next Tuesday.
[14:50] Asha: Agreed.
[14:54] Maya: I'll schedule the initial weekly sync and put the drive and SOW in the invite.
[15:05] Jordan: Great, thanks all — talk soon.
[15:10] (end)
notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions; product names may be slightly off in speaker text (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Dedicated'). Security pack and onboarding playbook referenced as links rather than embedded documents.
